subject.title: v2026.6.8: plugin_state_entries SQLite database corruption — session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released

question: Should OpenClaw add availability-first shared SQLite corruption recovery for openclaw.sqlite now, or first prove the takeover-to-corruption cause before changing shared-state behavior?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the right outcome changes data-retention, recovery, WAL/checkpoint, and session-lock policy for a shared persisted store used by multiple runtime surfaces.

options.title: Define shared-state recovery first
options.body: Choose a quarantine/preserve/fresh-state policy for malformed openclaw.sqlite, then implement recovery with focused plugin-state and task-state regression proof.

options.title: Prove the corruption cause first
options.body: Keep runtime fail-closed behavior while maintainers collect preserved DB sidecars, integrity traces, and a live takeover-to-corruption reproduction.

options.title: Split into existing trackers
options.body: Close this only if maintainers decide https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71689 plus the session-takeover trackers fully own the remaining work.

recommendation.title: Define shared-state recovery first
recommendation.body: Choose a quarantine/preserve/fresh-state policy for malformed openclaw.sqlite, then implement recovery with focused plugin-state and task-state regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for shared SQLite ownership is the database-first refactor and plugin-state migration introduced through PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78595.
